guides.title: How to Manage Multiple Gmail Accounts in One Inbox
guides.description: Compare Gmail account switching, mobile All inboxes, forwarding and Chrome extensions. Follow a practical guide to managing multiple Gmail accounts with Difmeil.
guides.lead: Personal email, client work, a side project. A shared inbox view can help you see what needs attention without checking each account in turn. The right setup depends on where you read your mail and how you want to handle it.
guides.quick: On a phone, use All inboxes in the Gmail app. On a computer, Gmail lets you switch between accounts, but that does not combine their inboxes. To bring incoming copies into one Gmail account, use forwarding. For a combined view that works with the original Gmail accounts in Chrome, consider an extension such as Difmeil.

sections.label: Choose your setup
sections.html:
First, decide what “one inbox” should mean

There are two different goals here. You might want a shared view: messages stay in their own accounts, but you read and manage them through one interface. Or you might want mail delivered to a main account: new messages from other addresses arrive there as forwarded copies.

Imagine you have personal, freelance and project Gmail accounts. Seeing all three together helps you triage the day. Keeping their identities clear matters just as much: archiving a project message should affect the right mailbox, and a client reply should come from your work address.

  • Mostly on your phone? Start with Gmail’s own combined mobile view.
  • Only checking a second account occasionally? Account switching may be enough.
  • Want new mail delivered to a primary Gmail address? Consider forwarding.
  • Need to manage the original accounts together on a computer? Consider a multi-account extension or email client.

A unified view does not merge Google identities, Drive files, account settings or storage quotas. You still own and sign in to each account separately.

sections.label: Gmail on desktop
sections.html:
Option 1: switch between Gmail accounts on desktop

Google supports signing in to several accounts in the same browser session. Open Gmail, select your profile picture or initial, add another account and sign in. Use that menu to choose the mailbox you want. You do not need to sign out each time.

This is a sensible choice when you prefer separate inboxes. You can keep mailboxes in separate tabs, or use Chrome profiles when you want a broader separation of browser activity. The tradeoff is that checking every inbox remains a separate task.

“Multiple Inboxes” is a different feature

Gmail’s desktop Multiple Inboxes layout builds sections using searches or labels within the mailbox you are viewing. It is useful for organizing that mailbox; it does not, by itself, connect separate Google accounts. Likewise, signing in to several accounts does not create the mobile app’s All inboxes view on the web.

Google’s documentation: sign in to multiple accounts and Gmail inbox layouts.

sections.label: All inboxes on mobile
sections.html:
Option 2: use All inboxes in the Gmail mobile app

Gmail for Android, iPhone and iPad has a built-in combined view. Add your Gmail accounts through your profile menu using Add another account, then choose Google and sign in. Once added, open the menu at the top left and select All inboxes.

This is often the easiest starting point if you handle email on your phone. It shows inbox mail together without forwarding it to a main address. Adding accounts in the app does not create a combined inbox at mail.google.com on your computer.

Official instructions: Gmail for Android and Gmail for iPhone and iPad.

sections.label: Forwarding to one account
sections.html:
Option 3: forward new messages to a main Gmail account

Forwarding suits people who want one destination for new mail and are comfortable managing copies. In each source Gmail account, open Settings → See all settings → Forwarding and POP/IMAP (or Forwarding). Add the destination address, complete verification there, then return to the source settings to enable forwarding and save. Choose what happens to the source copy.

Automatic forwarding covers new mail except spam, rather than moving your existing history. Filters can forward selected messages. Reading or archiving a forwarded copy does not synchronize that action back to the original mailbox.

Check the address you reply from

Forwarding does not configure the sending identity. If you want replies to use another Gmail address you own, set up and verify Gmail’s Send mail as separately, then check the From address before sending.

See Google’s forwarding instructions and Send mail as guidance. For a work or school account, check your organization’s forwarding policy.

Following an older tutorial?

Google is retiring Gmailify and POP-based “Check mail from other accounts” for third-party accounts. Its published timeline says new users are no longer supported after the first quarter of 2026; existing users can continue until January 2027. These changes are distinct from Gmail-to-Gmail forwarding and the mobile All inboxes view. Check Google’s current transition guidance before relying on an old POP setup.

sections.label: Browser extensions
sections.html:
Option 4: use a browser extension for a unified Gmail view

A multi-account extension can give you a shared workspace while keeping messages associated with their original accounts. Before installing one, check which providers it supports, which mail actions it offers, how authorization works and which features require payment. An unread counter alone is different from a full inbox you can work in.

Where Difmeil fits

Difmeil is a Chrome extension with a quick toolbar popup and a full-page inbox. It brings connected Gmail accounts together, lets you switch to an individual account and provides notifications across accounts.

You can read messages, mark them read or unread, archive them or move them to trash. It also supports composing, replying and forwarding. These are actions on the connected Gmail mailbox, rather than on a forwarded copy. Use the full-page search for searching across accounts; the popup’s search is limited to emails already loaded.

The free plan supports up to three accounts, the unified inbox, the full-page reader, search and basic notifications. Pro adds more accounts and advanced personalization and notification controls. Check the current plan comparison for details.

Difmeil is a practical fit if your daily work happens in Chrome and your accounts use Gmail. It is not a mobile app or a client for Outlook, Yahoo or general IMAP accounts. If you need multiple providers, look for a client that explicitly supports them. We make Difmeil; the alternatives here may suit your workflow better.

sections.html:
Compare the ways to manage multiple Gmail accounts

Choose based on the workflow you need, rather than the number of accounts alone. The important distinction is whether you are switching mailboxes, viewing them together or collecting copies.

On a small screen, scroll the comparison sideways. With a keyboard, focus the table area and use the arrow keys.

For example, if you only want to catch up during your commute, the mobile app may already solve the problem. If you spend the day processing personal and client mail at a desk, a shared desktop view avoids repeatedly revisiting the same account menus.

sections.label: Set up Difmeil
sections.html:
How to set up Difmeil with multiple Gmail accounts

Use these steps in Chrome on a computer. The control names below are from Difmeil’s English interface; Google’s sign-in screens can vary with your account and security settings.

  1. Install from the official listing

    Open Difmeil in the Chrome Web Store, choose Add to Chrome and review Chrome’s installation prompt. Confirm if you want to proceed. Open Difmeil from Chrome’s Extensions menu; you can pin its icon for easier access.

  2. Add your first Gmail account

    Click the Difmeil icon. In the initial Connect your first account view, select Add an account. This starts Google OAuth: choose the Google account you want to connect and complete any sign-in or two-step verification Google requests.

  3. Review Google’s access request

    Review the consent screen before approving. The current implementation requests basic identity information, permission to read and manage Gmail messages, permission to send mail, and read-only access to Google’s “Other contacts” for sender photos and recipient suggestions. These support the inbox, mail actions and composing. Difmeil does not ask you to type your Google password into the extension; sign-in happens with Google.

    Read the privacy policy if you want to understand data handling first. Mail requests go between your browser and Google. An authorization service exchanges and refreshes tokens without storing them. If a managed account blocks access, ask your administrator about the policy.

  4. Connect the other accounts

    After the first account connects, open the popup’s account controls and choose Add an account again. Authorize each additional Google account separately. Check the account you select each time; being signed in to Gmail in Chrome does not automatically grant Difmeil access. The full-page sidebar also has an Add account control.

  5. Open the combined inbox

    Choose Open full view in the popup, then All accounts in the full-page sidebar to work across your connected accounts. Select an individual account when you want to focus on it. Start with a few recent messages and check the account identity before applying actions.

  6. Read, act and adjust notifications

    Open a message to read it. Use the read/unread, archive or trash actions as needed; check the From account when composing or replying. Open Settings to review Notifications and the per-account notification switches in My accounts. Basic notifications are available on the free plan; advanced rules and do-not-disturb schedules require Pro.

You can continue opening Gmail directly when you need it. Installing Difmeil does not require setting up automatic forwarding or replacing your existing Gmail addresses.

sections.label: A daily workflow
sections.html:
A simple routine for working across accounts

A shared inbox is most useful when it gives you a clear next action. Try this routine before adding more rules or changing your whole email setup.

  • Scan together, focus separately. Use All accounts to spot urgent messages, then select your work account for a focused session.
  • Check identity before sending. A personal conversation and a client request can sit next to each other. Look at the account and recipient before replying.
  • Archive after deciding. Keep the inbox for messages that still need attention, rather than using unread status as your only task list.
  • Be selective about alerts. Enable notifications for accounts where interruptions are useful. If Gmail or another mail app is also notifying you, review both to avoid duplicate alerts.
  • Test your setup. Send yourself a harmless test message, confirm which account receives it, and verify that your chosen action appears in that account in Gmail.

sections.label: Troubleshooting
sections.html:
If an account or message is missing

The combined view only shows one account

Check that you connected each account through Google, rather than only signing in to Gmail in a browser tab. In Difmeil, select All accounts and check whether an account is hidden from the inbox. Clear any account or unread filters that could narrow the list.

An account asks to reconnect

Complete the offered reconnection flow with the correct Google account. If authorization fails, read Google’s error message; an organization policy or a withdrawn permission may require a different next step. Do not repeatedly change passwords just because a mailbox needs authorization again.

You cannot find an older message

The popup searches loaded messages. Try the full-page Gmail search for a broader lookup, or open the original account in Gmail to confirm that the message exists there. Forwarding, by contrast, does not bring your entire past mailbox into the destination automatically.

You are not receiving notifications

Check Difmeil’s global and per-account notification settings, then Chrome and your operating system’s notification settings. Quiet modes can suppress alerts. Notifications help you notice incoming mail; they should not be your only way to check an important mailbox. For product issues, use Difmeil support.

sections.label: FAQs
sections.html:
Frequently asked questions

Can I combine two Gmail accounts without merging them?

Yes. Gmail mobile’s All inboxes and a multi-account interface such as Difmeil let you view accounts together while keeping their identities separate. This does not merge the Google accounts or their storage.

Where is All inboxes in Gmail on my computer?

Gmail’s web interface offers account switching and inbox layouts, including Multiple Inboxes. It does not offer the same cross-account All inboxes view described in Google’s mobile instructions. Use the Gmail app on a phone, forwarding for incoming copies, or a desktop multi-account interface.

Do I need to forward my email to use Difmeil?

No. You authorize each Gmail account with Google OAuth. Difmeil works with those connected accounts, so a forwarding rule is not part of its setup.

Can I reply from the right Gmail address?

Difmeil supports replies and composing from connected accounts. Check the sending account before sending. If you instead collect forwarded messages in one Gmail mailbox, configure Gmail’s Send mail as separately for another address you own.

Is Difmeil free for multiple accounts?

The free plan supports up to three Gmail accounts, a unified inbox, full-page reading, search and basic notifications. More accounts and advanced notification and personalization features require Pro. See the plan comparison.

Does Difmeil support Outlook or work on my phone?

Difmeil is a Chrome extension for Gmail accounts. It is not a mobile app and does not connect Outlook, Yahoo or general IMAP mailboxes. Gmail’s mobile app or a client with explicit provider support may suit those needs.

Can I use a work or school Gmail account?

A Google Workspace Gmail account may be subject to your organization’s third-party access rules. Check with your administrator if Google blocks authorization. Do not assume that owning the address means you can override those policies.

guides.title: How to Get Notifications from Multiple Gmail Accounts
guides.description: Set up notifications for multiple Gmail accounts on desktop and mobile. Compare Gmail alerts, Chrome permissions and Difmeil’s free and Pro controls.
guides.lead: You can be signed in to several Gmail accounts and still miss an important message. The solution is to check how each account sends alerts, what your device allows, and which notifications actually deserve your attention.
guides.quick: You do not have to keep switching accounts to receive alerts. On desktop, configure Gmail’s desktop notifications for each mailbox and allow notifications in the browser and operating system. On mobile, review notification settings for every account in the Gmail app. In Chrome, Difmeil offers another approach: connect the accounts once and manage their notifications alongside a unified inbox.

sections.label: Gmail on desktop
sections.html:
Start with Gmail’s own desktop notifications

Account switching and notification delivery are separate things. You can stay signed in to several Google accounts; viewing one mailbox does not mean the others have been signed out. What matters is whether each mailbox has alerts configured and whether the browser can show them.

  1. Open the Gmail account you want to configure.
  2. Go to Settings → See all settings, then find Desktop notifications.
  3. Choose new-mail or important-mail alerts and save your changes.
  4. Allow the site to notify you if the browser requests permission. Repeat the Gmail setting for the other accounts.

Google describes these alerts for Gmail opened and signed in within a supported browser. Do not assume they will arrive with Gmail closed. With inbox categories enabled, new-mail alerts cover Primary; important-mail alerts use Gmail’s importance classification. See Google’s desktop notification instructions.

For an occasional second mailbox, this may be all you need. Before installing anything, test your current setup with a new message to each account and see whether it meets your needs.

sections.label: Chrome and device permissions
sections.html:
Check the browser and operating system too

Gmail’s notification preference is one layer. Chrome’s site permission and your operating system’s notification settings are others. A mail setting cannot override a blocked browser permission or a device’s quiet mode.

For Gmail website alerts in Chrome, open Settings → Privacy and security → Site settings → Notifications and review the permission for Gmail. You can also inspect the permission through the site-information control beside the address bar. Check that your operating system allows Chrome notifications, then review Focus or Do Not Disturb settings.

Chrome may remove permissions from unused sites, so recheck the site permission if alerts used to work. This website permission is different from an extension’s notification capability: allowing Gmail’s site does not configure Difmeil’s per-account switches. Read Chrome’s notification guidance for the current controls.

A useful test is to keep Gmail open, turn off device quiet mode temporarily and send one harmless message to each mailbox. If only one account stays silent, investigate its settings first; if every account stays silent, inspect the shared browser or device layer.

sections.label: Gmail on Android and iPhone
sections.html:
On mobile, configure every Gmail account

The Gmail app can notify you about more than one account. Review the settings for each account you added; the account currently visible on screen is not the only one that can receive alerts.

Android

In Gmail, open the menu, go to Settings, select an account and review Email notifications. For label-specific alerts, review that label’s synchronization and notification settings. If nothing arrives, check Gmail sync and Android’s app notification permissions. Google’s Android instructions explain the available levels.

iPhone and iPad

Allow Gmail notifications in the device settings, then review Email notifications inside Gmail’s settings for each account and choose a level that suits you. See Google’s iPhone and iPad instructions.

All inboxes is a reading view, not a master notification switch. Bringing messages together in that view does not replace per-account alert preferences. Mobile notifications and desktop notifications also need separate setup; changing one should not be treated as a way to configure the other.

sections.label: Compare your options
sections.html:
Which notification setup fits your workflow?

Choose where you want to be interrupted before choosing a tool. A phone alert may be enough for occasional mail; a desktop workspace can be more useful when you need to act on messages immediately.

On small screens, scroll the table sideways. Keyboard users can focus the table area and use the arrow keys.

Ways to receive alerts from several Gmail accounts
ApproachWhat it offersWhat to consider
Gmail in the browserNative desktop alerts with account-specific mail preferencesCheck every mailbox’s setting, site permission and device settings; Google documents alerts with Gmail open
Gmail mobile appAlerts for multiple accounts on a phone or tabletPer-account setup, app permissions and sync; separate from desktop
Forwarding to one accountAlerts from the destination mailbox for incoming forwarded copiesSource state stays separate; destination filters and notification rules apply
Difmeil for ChromeMulti-account notifications plus a unified Gmail inboxInstall and authorize accounts; Chrome must be running. Free up to three accounts; advanced controls require Pro
A desktop email clientA dedicated app that may support several providersVerify provider support, background behavior, cost and permissions for the client you choose

Forwarding can make sense if you already want a single delivery address. It is less suitable if you expect notification and read state to stay coordinated across the source mailboxes. Our guide to managing multiple Gmail accounts explains that distinction.

Browser extensions also vary: some show a counter, while others let you read and manage messages. We make Difmeil; use Gmail’s native settings if they already meet your needs.

sections.label: Set up Difmeil notifications
sections.html:
Set up notifications across your accounts in Difmeil

Difmeil is a Chrome extension for Gmail accounts. It checks connected mailboxes in the background and can show native system notifications without a Gmail tab open. It uses periodic checks, so alerts are not guaranteed to be instant. Chrome needs to be running, the extension enabled, and the account authorized.

  1. Install the official extension

    Open Difmeil in the Chrome Web Store, choose Add to Chrome and review the installation prompt. Open Difmeil from Chrome’s Extensions menu; pin it if you want quick access.

  2. Connect each account with Google

    Select Add an account in the popup and complete Google OAuth for the Gmail account you want to use. Repeat through the account controls for your other accounts. Sign-in happens with Google; do not enter your password into the extension. For the full walkthrough, see connecting multiple Gmail accounts.

    Review the consent request: the implementation asks for basic identity information, Gmail read/manage and send permissions, and read-only access to Other contacts for sender photos and recipient suggestions. Difmeil is an email client as well as a notifier, so access is broader than a simple counter. Read the privacy policy before authorizing. Mail requests go between the browser and Google; an authorization service exchanges and refreshes tokens without storing them.

  3. Enable the alerts you want

    Open Settings → Notifications and review the main notification switch. In My accounts, check the notification switch for each connected account. An account hidden from the inbox is excluded from notifications too, so keep the accounts you want monitored visible.

  4. Check device settings and test

    Allow Chrome notifications in your operating system and review its quiet modes. Leave Chrome running and send a new test message to each account. Use a fresh test message: existing unread messages may already have been notified or excluded by settings; unread counts do not guarantee a new alert.

  5. Choose how to act on mail

    The toolbar popup gives a quick view; Open full view opens the full-page inbox. Select All accounts to see messages together or select one account to focus. Read, reply, mark messages read, archive or move them to trash as needed.

Avoid running two noisy alert systems by accident. Once you have tested the setup, decide whether you want Gmail website alerts, Difmeil alerts or both. Turning one off is a workflow choice, not a requirement for the other to function.

sections.label: Free and Pro controls
sections.html:
What is free, and what requires Pro?

The free plan supports up to three Gmail accounts, a unified inbox, full-page reading, search and basic notifications. You can enable or disable notifications globally and for individual accounts.

Pro supports more accounts and adds advanced notification controls: do-not-disturb schedules, sender and subject rules, category filters and additional per-account overrides. If your priority is simply noticing mail from two or three accounts, start with the basic controls. If you need client messages to interrupt you while routine updates stay quiet, review the advanced rules.

Pro preferences are retained when access expires, but premium rules stop applying; the free controls remain available. Review your alert setup after a plan change rather than assuming an old premium filter is still active. The current plan comparison is the reference for included features.

Start with a small number of useful alerts. For example, keep one work account enabled during a focused session and silence a low-priority project account. More notifications are not always a better setup.

sections.label: Fix missing or duplicate alerts
sections.html:
Troubleshoot one layer at a time

Only one account is silent

Confirm that it is connected and authorized. Check its own notification switch, whether it is hidden, and any applicable rules. If Gmail itself is silent, inspect that account’s Gmail notification level and mail categories. Use a fresh test message instead of expecting an old unread message to trigger again.

All accounts are silent

Check the global notification switch, operating system permissions and quiet mode. In Difmeil, confirm that Chrome is running, the extension is enabled and you have a network connection. Periodic checking can be delayed by browser or device conditions; do not rely on email alerts as a guaranteed real-time channel.

You receive duplicate alerts

Identify which apps sent them. Gmail, Difmeil and a phone can each alert you about the same message. Disable the redundant source if you do not need it, rather than disconnecting a working account.

A rule seems to ignore an important message

Review the rule against the message’s sender, subject and category. In Difmeil, blocked senders take precedence over inclusion rules, and a read message is not notified. When troubleshooting, simplify the rules first, then reintroduce them one at a time. If you need help, contact Difmeil support without sending private message bodies.

sections.label: Notification FAQs
sections.html:
Frequently asked questions

Can Gmail notify me about two accounts at the same time?

Yes. Configure each account’s notification preferences. On mobile, review each added account in Gmail and allow app notifications. On desktop, check Gmail’s mailbox settings, browser permission and device settings.

Do I have to switch to an account to get its notifications?

No. Switching the mailbox you are viewing is different from configuring its alerts. Keep the relevant accounts signed in or connected, and check the conditions of the app you use.

Does Difmeil need Gmail tabs open?

No. Its background checks do not require an open Gmail tab. Chrome must be running, Difmeil enabled and the account connected. Alerts depend on periodic checks and device notification settings.

Will Difmeil notify me if Chrome is completely closed?

Do not expect that. Difmeil runs as a Chrome extension, not as a separate desktop notification service. Keep Chrome running when you want it to check your mail.

Can I mute just one Gmail account?

Yes. Difmeil’s basic per-account notification switch is available on the free plan. Advanced per-account overrides and notification schedules require Pro. Gmail mobile also has account-specific notification preferences.

Why do I see unread messages but receive no alert?

An unread count is not a promise of a new notification. A message may already have been notified, read before a check or excluded by settings. Use a fresh message to test the setup.

Does All inboxes turn on notifications for every mobile account?

No. It combines the reading view. Check notification settings for every account and the Gmail app’s device permission separately.
